Q.1 How has the distribution of content ratings changed over time?

In [5]:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load dataset
df = pd.read_csv("/content/netflix_titles.csv")

# Convert date_added to datetime
df['date_added'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date_added'], errors='coerce')

# Extract year
df['year_added'] = df['date_added'].dt.year

# Remove missing years or ratings
df = df.dropna(subset=['year_added', 'rating'])

# Group by year and rating
rating_trend = df.groupby(['year_added', 'rating']).size().reset_index(name='count')

# Pivot to make ratings as columns
rating_pivot = rating_trend.pivot(index='year_added', columns='rating', values='count').fillna(0)

# Plot the graph
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 7))
rating_pivot.plot(kind='line', figsize=(14, 7))

plt.title("Distribution of Content Ratings Over Time")
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Number of Titles Added")
plt.legend(title="Content Rating", bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1))
plt.grid(True)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load dataset
df = pd.read_csv("/content/netflix_titles.csv")

# Clean release year column
df['release_year'] = pd.to_numeric(df['release_year'], errors='coerce')

# Drop missing values
df = df.dropna(subset=['release_year', 'type'])

# ---------------------------
# 1️⃣ Boxplot (Best for visual comparison)
# ---------------------------
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='type', y='release_year')
plt.title("Distribution of Release Year by Type")
plt.xlabel("Content Type")
plt.ylabel("Release Year")
plt.grid(True, axis='y')
plt.show()

# ---------------------------
# 2️⃣ Summary statistics
# ---------------------------
print("Summary Statistics by Content Type:")
print(df.groupby('type')['release_year'].describe())

# ---------------------------
# 3️⃣ Scatter + jitter (age vs. type)
# ---------------------------

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.stripplot(data=df, x='type', y='release_year', jitter=True, alpha=0.6)
plt.title("Spread of Release Years for Movies vs TV Shows")
plt.xlabel("Content Type")
plt.ylabel("Release Year")
plt.grid(True, axis='y')
plt.show()

3.Can we identify any trends in content production based on the release year vs. the year added to Netflix?

In [9]:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load dataset
df = pd.read_csv("/content/netflix_titles.csv")

# Clean date_added column
df['date_added'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date_added'], errors='coerce')
df['year_added'] = df['date_added'].dt.year

# Clean release year
df['release_year'] = pd.to_numeric(df['release_year'], errors='coerce')

# Drop missing values
df = df.dropna(subset=['release_year', 'year_added'])

# ------------------------------
# 1️⃣ Scatterplot with Trend Line
# ------------------------------
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.regplot(data=df, x='release_year', y='year_added', scatter_kws={'alpha':0.2})
plt.title("Relationship Between Release Year and Year Added to Netflix")
plt.xlabel("Release Year")
plt.ylabel("Year Added to Netflix")
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

# ------------------------------
# 2️⃣ Heatmap (counts)
heatmap_data = df.groupby(['release_year', 'year_added']).size().reset_index(name='count')

heatmap_matrix = heatmap_data.pivot(
    index="release_year",
        columns="year_added",
            values="count"
            ).fillna(0)

plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))
sns.heatmap(heatmap_matrix, cmap="viridis")
plt.title("Heatmap of Release Year vs Year Added to Netflix")
plt.xlabel("Year Added")
plt.ylabel("Release Year")
plt.show()


# ------------------------------
# 3️⃣ Lag Analysis (How old is content when Netflix adds it?)
# ------------------------------
df['lag_years'] = df['year_added'] - df['release_year']

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.histplot(df['lag_years'], bins=40, kde=True)
plt.title("Distribution of Lag (Years Between Release and Netflix Addition)")
plt.xlabel("Years Between Release and Netflix Addition")
plt.ylabel("Number of Titles")
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

# Summary statistics for lag
print("Lag (years) summary:")
print(df['lag_years'].describe())

Q4. What are the most common word pairs or phrases in content descriptions?

In [12]:
import pandas as pd
from nltk.corpus import stopwords
from nltk.tokenize import word_tokenize
from nltk import FreqDist, bigrams
import nltk

# Download required NLTK resources
nltk.download('punkt')
nltk.download('punkt_tab')
nltk.download('stopwords')

# Load dataset
df = pd.read_csv("/content/netflix_titles.csv")

# Combine all descriptions into one text
text = " ".join(df['description'].astype(str))

# Tokenize
words = word_tokenize(text.lower())

# Remove stopwords and keep only alphabetic tokens
stop_words = set(stopwords.words('english'))
words = [w for w in words if w.isalpha() and w not in stop_words]

# Generate bigrams
bigram_list = list(bigrams(words))

# Frequency distribution
bigram_freq = FreqDist(bigram_list)

# Top 20 bigrams
top_bigrams = bigram_freq.most_common(20)

# Display results
for pair, freq in top_bigrams:
    print(f"{pair} : {freq}")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

pairs = [' '.join(pair) for pair, freq in top_bigrams]
counts = [freq for pair, freq in top_bigrams]

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.barh(pairs, counts)
plt.title("Top 20 Most Common Word Pairs in Descriptions")
plt.xlabel("Frequency")
plt.ylabel("Word Pair")
plt.gca().invert_yaxis()
plt.show()

Q.5 Who are the top directors on Netflix?

In [15]:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load dataset
df = pd.read_csv("/content/netflix_titles.csv")

# Prepare directors: remove NaNs, split multiple directors, explode
df = df.copy()
df['director'] = df['director'].fillna('').astype(str)
df = df[df['director'].str.strip() != '']   # drop rows with empty director
df['director'] = df['director'].str.split(r',\s*')   # split on comma + optional space
df = df.explode('director')
df['director'] = df['director'].str.strip()

# Optional: normalize case (uncomment if you want case-insensitive merging)
# df['director'] = df['director'].str.title()

# Count titles per director
director_counts = df['director'].value_counts().rename_axis('director').reset_index(name='title_count')

# Top N directors to visualize
TOP_N = 20
top_directors = director_counts.head(TOP_N)['director'].tolist()

# 1) Horizontal bar chart - Top 20 directors
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
sns.barplot(
    data=director_counts.head(TOP_N),
        y='director', x='title_count',
            palette='tab20'
            )
plt.title(f"Top {TOP_N} Directors by Number of Titles (Netflix Dataset)")
plt.xlabel("Number of Titles")
plt.ylabel("")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

            # 2) Stacked bar chart by type (Movie vs TV Show) for the top directors
            # Filter original exploded df for top directors and group by director & type
df_top = df[df['director'].isin(top_directors)]
grouped = df_top.groupby(['director', 'type']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)

            # Reindex rows to ensure same order as top list
grouped = grouped.reindex(top_directors)

            # Plot stacked bars
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
grouped.plot(kind='barh', stacked=True, figsize=(12,8))
plt.title(f"Breakdown of Top {TOP_N} Directors by Content Type (Movie vs TV Show)")
plt.xlabel("Number of Titles")
plt.ylabel("")
plt.legend(title="Type", bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.gca().invert_yaxis()  # keep the top director at top
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

            # 3) Print a table with counts and percent of total titles (for context)
total_titles_in_dataset = df.shape[0]
summary = director_counts.copy()
summary['percent_of_dataset'] = (summary['title_count'] / total_titles_in_dataset * 100).round(2)
print(f"Total titles considered (after exploding directors & dropping missing): {total_titles_in_dataset}\n")

            # Show top 20 table
display(summary.head(TOP_N))
